evidence: The only shipped data file is task/environment/assets/seed_data.json (the assets directory holds nothing else; no CSV/TSV). It is 149 bytes, LF line endings, no BOM, ASCII only, and parses with Python json to {'snippets': [], 'note': 'No saved snippets are supplied in this seed. Build a JavaScript and HTML playground with durable revision history.'}. Self-consistency: there are zero records, so there are no ids, foreign references, orphan rows, duplicate keys, dates or figures that could disagree. Synthetic/PII: the file names no person, organisation, e-mail, address or account, and holds no credential, token or URL (the Internal sheet annotation 'If task data itself contain credential flag it' is satisfied). Injection: the single free-text field 'note' is a plain restatement of the public ask; it carries no markup, no script, no instruction addressed to a judge, no claim about grading and no instruction to ignore the brief. Agreement with the public contract: instruction.md:3 says '/assets/seed_data.json describes the starting scope; there is no starter app to finish.' and integration.md:7 says '/assets/seed_data.json describes the starting scope and contains no user snippets or starter implementation.' Both match the bytes. The Dockerfile has 'COPY assets/ /assets/' and 'chmod -R a+rX /instructions /assets', identical to the frozen template Dockerfile, so the file the brief names is present and readable in the agent image. The template seed is the placeholder "CHANGE_ME"; the task replaced it and no placeholder remains. Consumers: the reference server.js and solve.sh never read /assets and insert rows only on user Save/Restore (server.js:61, 70, 114), so the golden's initial library is empty, matching 'snippets': []. No criterion or prompt quotes a seeded value; app_context.md:24 says 'the library may already hold records from earlier checks. Do not assume an empty library', so nothing depends on seed content. Counterexample search: a conforming app that ignores the seed file and a conforming app that reads it both begin with an empty library and are graded identically; a broken app gains nothing from the seed because it contains no record a criterion could be pre-satisfied by. Runtime evidence is not required to judge this static row; the scripted golden results on these bytes (results/runtime.json, persist-before.json, hashes verified) are consistent with an empty-seed start but were not needed for the verdict. Not measured by me: the private check-fixtures.py checker was not executed (applied by hand: the one JSON file parses and assets/ is copied), and I did not recompute the manifest input_sha256.
notes: Note (no action required): the seed's 'note' string contains an imperative sentence, 'Build a JavaScript and HTML playground with durable revision history.' It is addressed to the builder, repeats the public brief, and is never shown to a judge (the golden does not load the seed), so it is not an injection payload. A purely descriptive wording would be marginally cleaner.
Note: the seed is effectively a stub. Whether an empty seed is the best asset for the task is a row 13 / row 6 question, not a cleanliness defect under row 14.
Note: task.toml:2 lists /assets as an artifact and tests/test.sh:88 chmods /assets; both are template behaviour and consistent with the shipped file.
